claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that you live in the UK.

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I have one child - Alex, who is 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether they are in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** 

This includes things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to level 3
- A course that prepares them for an apprenticeship

It does **not** include:
- Paid apprenticeships
- Higher education (e.g., university degrees)
- Employment of 24 hours or more per week

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They actually work full-time now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, it appears you would **not** be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

- Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16, or for those aged 16-19 who remain in approved education or training.
- Since Alex is 18 and is no longer in approved education or training, and is working full-time, they no longer meet the criteria for Child Benefit.

Before I make my final assessment, I just want to confirm one thing:

**Has Alex recently left education or training (within the last 20 weeks), and if so, have they registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?**

This could potentially extend eligibility for a limited period.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they haven't done that. They just left school and went straight into work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on all the information you've provided, I can now make a final assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

### Summary

**Alex (age 18):** ❌ Not eligible

**Reason:** Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16, or for those aged 16 to 19 who remain in approved education or training. Since Alex is 18, has left school, is not in approved education or training, and is now working full-time, they no longer qualify for Child Benefit.

There was a potential option to extend eligibility for 20 weeks if Alex had registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services after leaving education, but since they went straight into work, this does not apply.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. If your circumstances change in the future, or if you have any other questions, please don't hesitate to ask.
